newsitem.title: USA: FOCUS-Fidelity's Pozen adds operational management.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Fidelity's Pozen adds operational management.

text.p: Fidelity Investments' newly- appointed president of its mutual fund division moved quickly Wednesday to install another layer of management to oversee day-to-day operations of Fidelity's stock funds.
Robert Pozen named three executives, including Abigail Johnson, daughter of Fidelity chairman Ned Johnson, to oversee the eight fund groups and focus on operational areas.

The three executives will "not only review funds but take off the back of the portfolio managers all the non-stock picking functions and allow the managers to concentrate on stock-picking," Pozen told Reuters in an interview.

William Hayes, chief operating officer of equity investments, and his assistant Bart Grenier had performed many of those functions on an informal basis, but Wednesday's annoucement formalizes the process.
Fidelity confirmed Wednesday that Hayes, 62, will retire by year-end and Grenier resigned earlier this month to join another firm.
"These are three people who are well known to the portfolio managers and I feel like they've already reacted very favorably to it," Pozen said.
In addition to Johnson, Fidelity named Robert Lawrence, head of Fidelity's high-income division, and Richard Spillane, former chief investment officer of Europe, to the new management team.
The three will focus on operational areas, including systems, trading, recruitment, research and human resources, as well as general fund oversight, Fidelity said.
"I think Bob is putting in place a management group to stabilize the ship," said Eric Kobren, publisher of the independent newsletter Fidelity Insight.

The three executives may also curtail any opposition among the portfolio managers to the appointment of Pozen, who was formerly Fidelity's legal counsel and never had any investment management experience, analysts said.

"I think having a little bit more hierarchy, though I know it's a bad word to a lot of people, I think these people will add value in supporting the fund managers, giving them the tools they need," he said.
Analysts said the additional help will help bolster the ranks of fund managers, who have been shaken by the departure of 24 portfolio heads in the last 18 months or so.
"Obviously, what everyone is waiting for is are the defections going to slow down," said Russel Kinnel, equity fund editor at Morningstar Mutual Funds.
The appointment of Johnson, Fidelity's largest shareholder, moves her closer to the chief executive's seat, but analysts still wonder if she will take the duties.
"I honestly do not believe that Abby knows what she wants to do and whether she wants to take over the company," Kobren said. "I think she's testing the waters and she's seeing what's going on."
Johnson will continue as group leader of the specialized growth group. Fidelity announced that Spillane will become group leader of the Income Growth group while overseeing the international group.
Johnson was not available for comment.
